trial.official_title: A Phase 3 Study of Dinutuximab Added to Intensive Multimodal Therapy for Children With Newly Diagnosed High-Risk Neuroblastoma

outcomes.description: EFS time is calculated from time of randomization to Arms A or B to first episode of disease relapse or progression, second malignancy, or death, or until last contact if no event has occurred.
outcomes.measure: Event free survival (EFS)

outcomes.description: The response rate will be calculated among all evaluable patients at end of Induction. Responders are defined as patients who achieve a \>= partial response per the revised 2017 International Neuroblastoma Response Criteria (INRC)
outcomes.measure: End of Induction (EOI) response rate
outcomes.time_frame: From randomization to end of extended Induction, up to 12 months

outcomes.description: OS time is calculated from time of randomization to Arms A or B until death, or until last contact if patient is alive.
outcomes.measure: Overall survival (OS)

outcomes.description: The proportion of patients with at least one grade 3 or higher non-hematologic toxicity or grade 4 or higher hematologic toxicity during protocol therapy, graded according to the National Cancer Institute Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events version 5.0, will be reported.
outcomes.measure: Incidence of adverse events

outcomes.description: Dinutuximab binding to pre-therapy patient tumor samples will be measured and categorized as high or low.
outcomes.measure: GD2 expression

outcomes.description: A series of univariate and multivariate Cox proportional hazards (for EFS and OS) and logistic regression (for responders vs. non-responders) models will be fit for patients in Arms A and B to evaluate the relationship between tumor and host factors (including tumor ALK and other somatic mutations, copy-number aberrations, gene fusions, gene expression, and pathogenic germline variants) and chemo-immunotherapy during Induction with outcome.
outcomes.measure: Association between tumor and host factors and outcomes

outcomes.description: Will be assessed by comparing the proportion of patients with detectable vs. non-detectable tumor markers (including circulating tumor deoxyribonucleic acid, circulating free DNA, circulating tumor cells, and immune function profiling) between Arms A and B during and after induction and post-consolidation therapy using chi-squared tests at each individual time point, and Cochran's Q across time points to determine if there is a consistent difference in proportions between arms across time. In addition, the tumor markers will be analyzed as continuous variables using longitudinal data analysis methodology such as mixed effects models or generalized estimating equations as appropriate.
outcomes.measure: Circulating biomarkers and markers of minimal residual disease

outcomes.description: The impact of early or late chemoimmunotherapy during Induction on the probability of the involvement of a specific disease site at first relapse will be evaluated using Fisher's exact test.
outcomes.measure: Patterns of failure

outcomes.description: A series of univariate and multivariate Cox proportional hazards (for EFS and OS) and logistic regression (for responders vs. non-responders) models will be fit for patients in arms A and B to evaluate the relationship between telomere maintenance mechanism and chemoimmunotherapy during Induction with outcome. Patients will be classified into 3 groups by telomere maintenance mechanism (TMM) based on messenger ribonucleic acid expression of TERT and analysis of telomeric DNA C-circles: telomerase (TERT) positive, alternative of lengthening of telomeres (ALT) positive, or no identified TMM.
outcomes.measure: Effect of telomere maintenance mechanisms

outcomes.description: Will descriptively summarize and compare the total Memorial Symptom Assessment Scale scores, total sub-domain scores, and individual symptom scores between patients randomized to receive dinutuximab during Induction (Arm B) to those of patients randomized to standard Induction (Arm A).
outcomes.measure: Functional and quality of life outcomes
outcomes.time_frame: At serial time points during Induction, Extended Induction, Post-Consolidation, and at the end of therapy

outcomes.description: Will be evaluated by descriptively comparing the successful delineation of histologic classification, MYCN amplification status, and ALK status via the traditional method of obtaining tissue for diagnosis, open surgical biopsy, versus the less invasive percutaneous core needle biopsy.
outcomes.measure: Adequacy of diagnostic biopsy specimens

outcomes.description: Kaplan-Meier curves of EFS and OS will be generated and used to calculate 3-year EFS and OS estimates. Associations between social determinants of health (SDOH) and survival outcomes and time to receipt of dinutuximab will be evaluated with univariate and multivariate Cox proportional hazard models. Log-binomial regression will be used to estimate risk ratios and 95% CI for the occurrence of dinutuximab consent to randomization and therapy receipt by SDOH exposure. Effect modification of outcomes as a function of poverty, stratified by race/ethnicity, will be explored.
outcomes.measure: Associations between family-reported adverse social determinants of health and both clinical outcomes and biology

outcomes.description: Scans will be given as input to a convolutional neural network trained to predict EOI response.
outcomes.measure: Develop and validate deep learning predictors of Induction response (imaging objective)
outcomes.time_frame: At diagnosis, EOI, during Extended Induction, and end of Extended Induction

outcomes.description: Will be assessed by calculating the percentage of patients receiving the same EOI institutional and centrally reviewed determination of overall response, individual response components (primary tumor, soft tissue and bone metastatic disease, and bone marrow metastatic disease), and PEIR and GEIR. In addition, Cohen's kappa will be calculated to evaluate the concordance in each of these response measures.
outcomes.measure: Compare institutional versus central determination of overall response, individual response components, and PEIR and GEIR determination (imaging objective)

outcomes.description: Will be addressed by calculating the proportion of treated patients with each late effect, including but not limited to impaired organ function, neuropsychiatric toxicity, and secondary malignancy. A 95% confidence interval will be placed on each proportion.
outcomes.measure: Incidence of late toxicities

outcomes.description: The cumulative incidence of local progression (CILP) in patients with complete response of the primary site at EOI and GEIR on this study will be compared to the CILP rate of 11.2±1.8% observed on ANBL0532 using Gray's test.
outcomes.measure: Reduced dose radiotherapy to the primary site clinical target volume (CTV) in patients with complete response of the primary site at EOI results in comparable local control relative to historical cohorts

outcomes.description: Will be evaluated by calculating the incidence of endothelial injury complications and non-relapse mortality within 100 days of transplant, transplant-associated thrombotic microangiopathy (TA-TMA), severe TA-TMA, and sinusoidal obstruction syndrome (SOS) on Arms A and B and comparing between arms with a chi-squared test. The impact of TA-TMA occurrence on the timing or exclusion of subsequent therapy and interventions utilized to treat the TA-TMA, and associations with outcomes (EFS and OS) will be assessed.
outcomes.measure: Post-transplant complications

outcomes.description: Log-rank tests will be used to explore the association between EOI response (using both the revised INRC and GEIR/PEIR classification) and individual response components (primary tumor, soft tissue and bone metastatic disease, and bone marrow metastatic disease) with outcome (EFS and OS).
outcomes.measure: Associations between end of induction (EOI) response and individual response components

outcomes.description: The proportion of patients in the analytic cohort for whom each particular IDRF and also the presence of any IDRF is absent prior to surgical resection will be computed. McNemar's test for paired observations will be applied to determine whether there is a difference in the proportion of each IDRF and any IDRF present before and after initial therapy, and conditional logistic regression will be used to compare between treatment arms A and B. The IDRF status after initial therapy and whether there has been a change from diagnosis will be associated with surgical outcome (complete vs. incomplete resection, presence or absence of surgical complications) using chi-squared tests, and compared between treatment arms A and B with the Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test. The association of IDRF status with presence or absence of local failure after primary tumor resection will also be evaluated using a chi-squared test, and compared between treatment arms A and B with the Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel.
outcomes.measure: Changes in image-defined risk factors (IDRF)

abstract: Ralstonia solanacearum is a globally distributed, soil-borne species complex that causes bacterial wilt in many economically important crops. Race 3 biovar 2 (R3b2) is a cold-tolerant, highly aggressive subgroup within this complex that is responsible for an estimated $1 billion in annual global losses. Because R3b2 remains exotic to North America, it is classified as a USDA Select Agent due to its high potential to devastate U.S. solanaceous crops and ornamental industries. However, current diagnostic methods for this pathogen involve trade-offs among cost, sensitivity, specificity, and ease of use, particularly for point-of-care (POC) detection in field settings. CRISPR-based detection platforms have recently emerged as promising tools for high-sensitivity POC diagnostics. Here we developed an isothermal recombinase polymerase amplification (RPA)/Cas12a assay for specific, sensitive and rapid detection of R3b2. By targeting a genomic region associated with the cool-virulence phenotype, the assay reliably differentiates R3b2 from plant hosts and other diverse R. solanacearum strains. Incorporation of a dual-guide RNA system and an 8-mer single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) fluorescent reporter further improved sensitivity and reduced detection time. Using dilution series of R3b2-spiked Pelargonium DNA extracts, the assay detected as few as 4 CFU per reaction. To facilitate POC applications, the system was adapted into a one-pot, contamination-resistan¬t format compatible with portable fluorescence readers such as Genie III device and P51 viewer. By improving both sensitivity and portability, this assay enhances current diagnostic capabilities and, pending validation in real-world conditions, supports early surveillance efforts aimed at preventing the introduction of R3b2 into the United States.

abstract: Double-stranded RNA (dsRNA) is a potent immunogenic impurity and its detection is a critical quality attribute in characterizing mRNA therapeutics. Standard analytical methods (e.g., sandwich ELISA) are only able to resolve the bulk presence of dsRNA and cannot characterize the different sub-species that may be present within a mRNA sample.. In this study, we use mass photometry (MP) as a single-molecule analytical platform for the simultaneous detection and characterization of dsRNA impurities in mRNA samples. We demonstrate how ionic strength can interfere with the stability of the mAb/dsRNA complex and measure the binding affinity (1 nM) under a set of parameters for reproducible characterization of the complex. We then leverage the J2 antibody to identify antibody/dsRNA complexes that then resolve dsRNA-positive species within an mRNA sample based on discrete molecular weight profiles. Furthermore, we introduce a novel MP assay that harnesses the repulsive surface chemistry of uncoated glass to exclude the bulk mRNA analyte to enable the use of higher loading concentrations to sensitively profile trace dsRNA impurities as antibody-bound species. This work establishes MP as a valuable next generation mRNA analytical tool for analyzing dsRNA byproducts within mRNA samples.

abstract: Neutralizing antibodies act rapidly against SARS-CoV-2, but monoclonal antibodies are costly to manufacture and single-domain antibodies are cleared rapidly. Here we evaluated an mRNA-lipid nanoparticle (LNP) platform encoding the neutralizing nanobody VHH 72 and optimized the carrier by raising DSPC from 10 to 40 mol% and the citrate buffer from 25 to 300 mM. Relative to 10%PC-25mM, 40%PC-300mM produced larger particles (approximately 193 versus 75 nm), lower polydispersity, high encapsulation efficiency and better mRNA preservation in 50% serum (approximately 80% versus 43% at 24 h). Molecular dynamics simulations of the two lipid compositions gave structural descriptors consistent with tighter packing at 40 mol% DSPC, but did not address free energy or the citrate effect. In HEK293T cells, 40%PC-300mM increased VHH 72-eGFP-positive cells at 24, 48 and 72 h and cell-associated fusion protein at 72 h. In CD-1 mice, DiD-associated fluorescence declined more slowly in blood and was higher in liver through 72 h and spleen through 48 h; a luciferase reporter showed higher organ expression and a whole-body advantage through day 5. Serum VHH 72 peaked later and higher with 40%PC-300mM, and neutralizing activity persisted through day 7. In K18-hACE2 mice challenged intraperitoneally or intratracheally 1, 3 or 7 days after treatment, 40%PC-300mM gave the lowest blood and lung pseudovirus reporter signals at day 3 and was the only treatment significantly below PBS at day 7. These data support formulation optimization as a way to improve mRNA protection, reporter expression and the duration of functional VHH 72 exposure. Because the study used reporter constructs, a lipophilic dye, pseudovirus and mice, it does not establish intact-LNP biodistribution or protection against authentic SARS-CoV-2 infection.

abstract: PRE-EMPT will assemble a cohort of 150 participants from three populations (low risk, intermediate risk, and high risk for self-harm). We will obtain clinical assessments, structural and functional MRI utilizing tasks pioneered by our team to assess cognitive control (CC) and emotion regulation (ER), and peripheral circular RNA (circRNA) levels to characterize the molecular brain states associated with behavioral risk. The clinical, imaging, and transcriptomic data will be fused and jointly analyzed to increase the accuracy of our risk prediction models. PRE-EMPT in three separate Aims will then prospectively assess three promising and innovative interventions for their potential to reduce suicidal ideation and alter activity in key neural networks: 1) neurofeedback (NF) using real-time fMRI with simultaneous electroencephalography (EEG), 2) a form of transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) called accelerated intermittent theta burst stimulation (aiTBS) with dose optimization through electric field modeling; and 3) psilocybin assisted therapy (PSI), with flexible dosing plan to maximize the depth of psychedelic experience. These therapies were chosen based on our team's prior work in all three interventions demonstrating rapid action and large effects.

description:
This is a first in human Phase I study of RNA-LP vaccines for newly diagnosed adult MGMT unmethylated (low level or undetected) glioblastoma (GBM) and pediatric patients with newly diagnosed HGG (pHGG). The phase I portion of the study will involve a dose-escalation study to identify the maximally tolerated dose (MTD). The GBM portion of the study is single site (UF) and the pediatric portion will be multisite.

This clinical trial will consist of three parts: Surgery, Radiation, and Immunotherapy. Surgery and chemoradiation will be standard of care for patients with GBM. Potentially eligible participants will be enrolled on a screening consent for the sterile collection of tumor material in a manner suitable for RNA extraction, amplification, and loading of lipid particles (LPs). Pediatric participants will have tumor material sent to the University of Florida (UF) from qualified PNOC sites. Adult GBM participants must have surgery for collection of tumor material at the University of Florida. Following surgical resection with confirmatory pathologic diagnosis, patients will be enrolled in the trial after informed consent has been obtained.

The RNA-LP vaccination will begin within 4 weeks following radiation and after review of post-radiation MRI (for baseline). After radiation patients will receive three RNA-LP vaccines every 2 weeks before beginning 12 cycles of adjuvant monthly RNA- LP vaccines for a total of 15 vaccines.

Participants may receive RNA-LP vaccines for up to 14 months.

Participants will be followed until death due to any cause. MRI and clinical evaluation for assessment of disease progression will be conducted every 3 months for the first-year post-immunotherapy and then every 6-12 months over the next 2 years.

outcomes.description: Potentially eligible participants will be enrolled on a screening consent for the sterile collection of tumor material in a manner suitable for RNA extraction, amplification, and loading of lipid particles (LPs). Tumor material will be sent to the University of Florida (UF) where tumor specific RNA-LP vaccines will be manufactured. Manufacturing feasibility will be determined based on the percentage of vaccines that are successfully manufactured in the DLT window during the first three vaccines. If two-thirds of vaccines are successfully manufactured with QA/QC clearance, we will conclude that RNA-LPs can be successfully manufactured.

outcomes.description:
A DLT will be defined as any immunotherapy-related (possible, probable or definite):

* Grade ≥ 3 non-hematologic toxicity that does not improve to ≤ Grade 2 within 72 hours; hepatic or renal dysfunction that does not improve to ≤ grade 2 within 7 days
* Grade ≥3 cytokine release syndrome that does not improve to ≤ Grade 2 within 72 hours
* Grade ≥ 3 encephalopathy as defined by the American Society for Transplantation and Cellular Therapy (ASTCT) Consensus Immune Effector Cell-Associated Encephalopathy criteriaGrade 3 or greater non-neurologic, non-hematologic toxicity
* Grade 3 neurologic toxicity that does not improve to Grade II or better within 7 days
* Grade 3-4 hematologic toxicity that does not improve to Grade 2 or better within 14 days
* Grade 3 autoimmune encephalomyelitis
* Grade 4 neurologic toxicity.
outcomes.measure: Safety of RNA-LP vaccine
outcomes.time_frame: First vaccine through 14 days after administration of the 3rd vaccine.

outcomes.description: The Phase I Stratum 1 dose-escalation study will be performed in up to 28 adult participants using a Bayesian optimal interval (BOIN) design with an initial embedded accelerated titration design (ATD) to efficiently identify the maximally tolerated dose (MTD). For the initial ATD, patients will be enrolled and treated in cohorts of size 1 starting at dose level -4 to dose level -1. After the first DLT is observed or if dose level 0 is reached without prior DLT in dose level -4 to -1, the study will expand to a BOIN design with a cohort size of 3 to identify the MTD. For the initial ATD, patients will be enrolled and treated in cohorts of size 1 starting at dose level -4 to dose level -1, and will expand to a cohort size of 3 after the first DLT is observed or at dose level 0. There are 8 dose levels to potentially be assessed including the possibility of 4 dose levels for the ATD and 4 for the BOIN.

abstract: Cisplatin-based chemotherapy constitutes the cornerstone of first-line treatment for muscle-invasive and metastatic bladder cancer (BCa); however, the frequent emergence of chemoresistance presents a formidable clinical obstacle. In the present study, by combining a systematic CRISPR-Cas9 E3 ligase library screen with drug sensitivity data from the GDSC database, DCST1 (DC-STAMP Domain Containing 1) was identified as a pivotal driver of cisplatin resistance. DCST1 expression was found to be markedly upregulated in chemoresistant BCa tissues, and its elevated expression served as an independent predictor of poor patient prognosis. Functionally, DCST1 deficiency sensitizes BCa cells to cisplatin in vitro and in vivo by triggering PANoptosis (simultaneous apoptosis, pyroptosis, and necroptosis). Mechanistically, DCST1 functions as an atypical E3 ubiquitin ligase to catalyze the K11/K27-linked polyubiquitination of NFAT5 at residue K450. This non-canonical ubiquitination stabilizes NFAT5 by preventing its lysosomal degradation and promotes its nuclear accumulation. Nuclear NFAT5 then transcriptionally activates SOD2, orchestrating an anti-PANoptotic program that ensures BCa cell survival under chemotherapeutic stress. Furthermore, through molecular docking and CETSA validation, digoxin was identified as a potent pharmacological inhibitor of NFAT5 that overcomes DCST1-mediated chemoresistance and synergistically restores cisplatin sensitivity. Collectively, these findings unveil a previously unrecognized ubiquitination-dependent mechanism of chemoresistance and establish the DCST1-NFAT5 signaling axis as a promising therapeutic target for overcoming drug resistance in BCa.

abstract:
BACKGROUNDS: Lysine crotonylation (LCR) is an emerging post-translational modification, yet its clinical significance and therapeutic relevance in clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) remain poorly understood.
METHODS: Multi-omics data were collected from public repositories. Consensus clustering based on 18 LCR-related genes (LCRGs) was performed to define molecular subtypes. Co-expression modules identified via WGCNA were integrated into 101 machine-learning combinations to establish a LCR-related signature (LCRS). The signature was evaluated for survival prediction, immune microenvironment characteristics, and drug response across multiple cohorts, complemented by single-cell RNA sequencing. Candidate therapeutic targets and compounds were screened using DepMap CRISPR dependency data and pharmacogenomic databases (CTRP and PRISM).
RESULTS: Two distinct molecular subtypes (C1 and C2) were identified, displaying significant differences in survival, immune infiltration, and signaling pathways. Integrating WGCNA hub genes with an optimal machine-learning framework yielded a robust 15-gene LCRS, which served as an independent prognostic factor in the TCGA cohorts. Single-cell analysis localized signature genes predominantly to endothelial cells. Pharmacogenomic profiling indicated higher sensitivity to sunitinib among high-risk patients, whereas low-risk patients displayed elevated sensitivity to axitinib and pazopanib. Furthermore, dependency screening prioritized CLCNKA as a key therapeutic target along with ten candidate compounds for high-risk patients.
CONCLUSIONS: This study establishes a robust LCR-related prognostic signature and nominates CLCNKA as a novel therapeutic vulnerability, offering actionable insights for personalized stratification and treatment in ccRCC.

abstract: Androgen receptor pathway inhibitors (ARPIs) prolong survival in prostate cancer, yet durable control is frequently lost through transcriptional adaptation and lineage plasticity. Whether environmental endocrine-disrupting chemicals can actively bias this trajectory and create tractable resistance dependencies remains unclear. Here we show that chronic low-dose exposure to triphenyl phosphate (TPP) induces exposure-conditioned, partially persistent and reversible enzalutamide tolerance in AR-positive prostate cancer cells, accompanied by increased colony formation. Tolerance persists initially after exposure withdrawal but declines during washout, and TPP rechallenge increases GR50 again. A pooled CRISPR screen across two genetic backgrounds converged on MEN1 as the most robust concordant hit, and genetic perturbation and rescue identified a MEN1 dependency that was most apparent in the TPP-conditioned tolerant state. Mechanistically, TPP induced NR1I2 and MEN1 mRNA, endogenous target genes, and PXR-associated reporter activity; antagonist-sensitive transcriptional responses, SPA70-mediated reversal of tolerance, and MEN1-locus regulatory-region visualization were consistent with engagement of a PXR/NR1I2-associated receptor program. Targeted chromatin profiling identified MEN1-dependent changes in H3K4me3, H3K27ac and accessibility at selected AR and plasticity-associated loci. TPP_long reduced H3K4me3 and accessibility at AR loci, while MEN1 CRISPRi opposed the major transcriptional and chromatin changes. In LNCaP-luc xenografts, TPP exposure attenuated enzalutamide-mediated tumor suppression, and MEN1 CRISPRi reduced tumor burden in the TPP + enzalutamide background. This reduction in enzalutamide control was not reproduced in the exploratory VCaP model under androgen deprivation. Together, these data support an exposure-conditioned receptor-to-chromatin model in which MEN1 supports an AR-low/plasticity-high adaptive state.

abstract: Simultaneous detection of dual microRNA biomarkers is crucial for accurate prognosis and treatment monitoring of cervical spondylosis, yet remains challenging due to the lack of stringent logic control and high-fidelity signal amplification. Herein, we report an AND-gate-controlled colorimetric assay that integrates target-recycling strand displacement amplification, CRISPR/Cas13a/crRNA-mediated trans-cleavage, and self-priming cyclic amplification for sensitive and specific analysis of two cervical spondylosis-associated miRNAs (miRNA-221 and miRNA-146a). Only when both targets are present does the cascade proceed, producing double-stranded amplicons that trigger SYBR Green I-catalyzed TMB oxidation, yielding a naked-eye-visible blue signal. The assay exhibits a broad linear range from 10 fM to 500 pM, a detection limit of 2.12 fM, excellent selectivity, and good repeatability. Importantly, we applied this method to clinically evaluate the therapeutic effect of auricular point pressing (ear acupressure), a traditional Chinese medicine intervention for cervical spondylosis. In a 4-week study of 20 patients, the treatment group receiving auricular point pressing showed significant downregulation of both miRNAs compared to baseline, while the control group showed no notable change. Results correlated well with RT-qPCR, confirming reliability. This logic-controlled CRISPR/Cas13a platform offers a robust, equipment-free strategy for early prognosis of cervical spondylosis and objective monitoring of auricular point pressing therapy.

abstract: APOBEC3 cytosine deaminases are major sources of cancer mutations. In lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD), APOBEC3 activity drives tumor evolution and therapy resistance, nominating these enzymes as therapeutic targets. Although APOBEC3A drives most APOBEC3-associated mutational signature burden across cancers, the relative contributions of individual paralogs in LUAD remain unclear. Here, we define the roles of endogenously misregulated APOBEC3 deaminases using CRISPR-Cas9 knockouts and whole-genome sequencing of 197 long-term propagated single-cell clones. APOBEC3 mutagenesis falls into three patterns, driven predominantly by APOBEC3A, by both APOBEC3A and APOBEC3B, or minimal despite detectable enzyme expression. Commonly used surrogate measures, including mRNA and protein levels and in vitro deaminase activity, do not predict these contributions. We also provide the first causal evidence that endogenous APOBEC3A generates the indel signature InD9a, linking it to uracil excision following cytosine deamination. These heterogeneous contributions highlight the need for biomarkers that resolve individual APOBEC3 activities to guide therapeutic targeting.

abstract: N-acetylgalactosamine (GalNAc)-modified extracellular vesicles (EVs) derived from hypoxic pancreatic cancer cells and loaded with annexin A2 (ANXA2) small interfering RNA (siRNA) were developed to modulate the immunosuppressive tumour microenvironment (TME). Characterisation confirmed successful surface modification and efficient siRNA loading in EVs with a diameter of approximately 100-120 nm. In vitro, these engineered EVs inhibited pancreatic cancer cell proliferation, migration and invasion and promoted apoptosis. Additional cargo-matched comparison showed that GalNAc-modified hypoxic EVs carrying ANXA2 siRNA produced stronger ANXA2 silencing and more pronounced anti-migratory, anti-invasive and pro-apoptotic effects than unmodified hypoxic EVs carrying the same siRNA. In a xenograft model, treatment suppressed tumour growth and improved survival. Multi-omics and immune analyses suggested suppression of the PI3K/AKT signalling pathway and remodelling of the immunosuppressive TME, as reflected by increased CD8+ T-cell infiltration, reduced tissue-associated immunoreactivity for interleukin-6 (IL-6), interleukin-10 (IL-10), and tumour necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α), and increased soluble interferon-gamma (IFN-γ), interleukin-2 (IL-2) and GM-CSF levels. These findings indicate that GalNAc-modified hypoxic EVs carrying ANXA2 siRNA can inhibit tumour progression and modulate the TME in pancreatic cancer, supporting their potential as a therapeutic delivery platform.

abstract: Delivery of CRISPR-Cas9 ribonucleoprotein (RNP) using synthetic materials can bypass the host translational machinery and limit the duration of genomic exposure, minimizing the risk of off-target mutations. Despite their advantages, lipid nanoparticle (LNP) platforms for CRISPR-Cas9 RNP delivery that achieve highly efficient editing at low doses remain limited. In the present study, we developed a library of ionizable lipids (ILs) and corresponding LNPs to enhance the delivery and editing efficiencies of CRISPR-Cas9 RNP complexes. Following comprehensive in vitro screening and formulation optimization, an optimal LNP candidate containing the C12A9 IL (denoted as LNPC12A9) was identified that achieved ∼90% EGFP disruption in HEK293T-EGFP cells at an RNP concentration of 30 nM and ∼60% at 15 nM. The editing performance was consistently observed at an RNP concentration of 15 nM when editing the Gcgr and HPRT1 genes across multiple hepatic cell lines. Moreover, coencapsulation of RNP and a single-stranded oligodeoxynucleotide (ssODN) template for homology-directed repair (HDR) within LNPC12A9 induced an HDR rate of 37.8%. Systemic administration of LNPC12A9 into C57BL/6J mice led to liver tropism and a total hepatic Pcsk9 gene disruption rate of 1.39%. In conclusion, this study provides insights into the construction of an LNP platform to improve the delivery efficiency of CRISPR-Cas9 RNP, thereby facilitating the development of LNPs for safe, precise, and tissue-specific Cas9 RNP-based genome editing therapies.

title: High-Throughput Screening of a Lipid Nanoparticle (LNP) Library Identifies Lead Formulations for CRISPR-Cas9 Ribonucleoprotein Delivery and Gene Editing.

abstract: Viral infections represent a major global health challenge due to the rapid emergence of new pathogens, increasing antiviral drug resistance and limited efficacy of traditional treatments against evolving viruses. Nanotechnology is a promising interdisciplinary approach to fighting viral diseases, which can perform direct viral inactivation, targeted drug delivery, immune modulation, vaccine development, rapid diagnostics, and prevention of infection. This review offers an in-depth and critical overview of the major antiviral nanoparticle platforms, including metallic, metal oxide, carbon-based, polymeric, lipid-based, and bio-inspired nanoparticles. In this article, we employ a comparative framework to systematically analyze classes of nanoparticles based on their physicochemical properties, molecular mechanisms of antiviral action, biomedical applications, and translational potential. Antiviral mechanisms are discussed within the framework of the viral life cycle, including the inhibition of viral attachment and entry, destruction of viral envelope and capsid integrity, suppression of intracellular viral replication, reactive oxygen species-mediated viral inactivation, immune-modulation, and nanoparticle-assisted therapeutic delivery. Moreover, the review critically discusses the increasing biomedical applications of antiviral nanoparticles in therapeutics, vaccine delivery, diagnostics, antiviral coatings, gene therapy and precision nanomedicine, while highlighting the clinically successful technologies such as lipid nanoparticle-based mRNA vaccines. Special attention is paid to the main obstacles in clinical translation, such as nanotoxicity, biodistribution, manufacturing scalability, regulatory challenges, and the lack of standard evaluation protocols. Finally, major knowledge gaps and future research priorities are highlighted, focusing on the design of multifunctional, clinically translatable and regulatory-compliant nanoplatforms. This review offers insights on antiviral nanomedicines and practical insights for the rational design and successful clinical translation of next-generation antiviral nanoparticle.

abstract: Immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) is an autoimmune disorder characterized by antibody-mediated platelet destruction and impaired regulatory T-cell (Treg) function, yet its molecular basis remains poorly defined. Here, we show that CD4+ naive T cells from patients with ITP exhibit diminished T-cell receptor (TCR) signaling and impaired in vitro Treg induction relative to healthy controls. RNA sequencing revealed widespread dysregulation of alternative splicing, most notably exon 8 skipping in LCK, a kinase central to TCR signaling and Treg differentiation. Using an LCK minigene combined with RNA pull-down mass spectrometry and RNA immunoprecipitation assays, we identified the splicing factor SRSF1 as a direct upstream regulator of LCK exon 8 skipping. Notably, SRSF1 expression was reduced in CD4+ naive T cells from patients with ITP, and its overexpression restored in vitro Treg induction capacity. Antisense oligonucleotide-mediated blockade of SRSF1 binding to LCK enhanced exon 8 skipping and attenuated TCR activation in Jurkat cells. Although murine Lck lacks the human-specific recursive splicing sites required for exon 8 exclusion, the adoptive transfer of CD4+ naive T cells expressing the exon 8-skipped murine Lck into CD61-knockout mice significantly reduced Treg proportions and platelet counts in an active ITP model. Mechanistically, Jurkat cells engineered to express only the exon 8-skipped LCK variant showed markedly reduced binding to ZAP70 and CD3ζ, which may partly account for the attenuated TCR signaling and downstream FOXP3 induction. Together, these findings define a novel SRSF1-LCK splicing axis that may regulate Treg development in ITP.

abstract: Since the discovery of the clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeat (CRISPR)-associated (Cas) system, genome-editing technologies have advanced rapidly, and the field has expanded substantially. In parallel, artificial intelligence (AI) has progressed at an unprecedented pace and is transforming genetic engineering. Early AI applications primarily addressed predictive tasks, including guide RNA (gRNA) activity, off-target effects, and editing outcomes for CRISPR-Cas nucleases, base editors, and prime editors. Recently, transformer-based protein language models (PLMs) and generative AI have expanded the role of AI beyond prediction to direct molecular design. Thus, AI-driven frameworks can now evolve genome-editing proteins, design molecular architectures, and generate de novo genome-editing enzymes. This review discusses how AI is reshaping genome engineering, from gRNA activity prediction to the design of next-generation editors.

title: Beyond prediction: The evolving role of artificial intelligence in genome editing.

abstract: The voltage-gated sodium channel NaV1.7 (SCN9A) is a genetically validated target for pain therapy, but achieving therapeutic isoform selectivity remains a formidable challenge for small-molecule inhibitors. Here, we overcome this bottleneck through a highly selective RNA-targeted strategy that dictates SCN9A alternative splicing. We first identified ASO50 as the most potent baseline candidate antisense oligonucleotide (ASO). Subsequent 5'-decoy (5D) sequence screening yielded an upgraded candidate, L9C-ASO50, which is engineered to competitively intercept U1 snRNA, achieving a cooperative spatial hindrance that robustly suppresses exon 5 recognition. This targeted exon exclusion introduces a frameshift that triggers robust, obligate transcript clearance via the nonsense-mediated mRNA decay (NMD) pathway, ensuring complete functional silencing without cross-reacting with homologous NaV channels. Mechanistically, we define the underlying cis-trans regulatory architecture, revealing a homeostatic tug-of-war where the RNA-binding protein ELAVL2 enforces exon inclusion, paradoxically antagonized by the canonical SR protein family. Crucially, CNS-restricted delivery of L9C-ASO50 produces profound and sustained mechanical and thermal analgesia. These findings establish splice-modulated transcript degradation as a viable therapeutic paradigm for chronic pain and provide a broadly applicable blueprint for engineering targeted RNA therapeutics.

abstract: The bacterium Rhodococcus equi is a common cause of severe pneumonia in foals worldwide. Foals are exposed to R. equi from birth and are most susceptible in the first weeks of life. In North America, control measures are limited to transfusion to newborn foals of hyperimmune plasma whose potency is assessed by surpassing a threshold of IgG against the virulence-associated protein A (VapA) of R. equi. Here we report results of vaccination of pregnant mares with mRNA encoding a GPI-anchored virulence-associated protein A (VapA) of R. equi induced VapA-specific IgG subisotypes transferred to their foals during the 63-day period after birth. Pregnant mares were randomly assigned to receive either VapA mRNA vaccine (n=10) at 8 and 10 months of gestation or no vaccine (n=10). Serum was collected from mares at 8 months of gestation (before vaccination for immunized mares) and {approx}24 hours after foaling and from foals at ages 1, 35, and 63 days. Mean relative concentrations of were low before immunization in all mares and did not change over time in unvaccinated mares; however, mean relative concentrations of anti-VapA IgG1, IgG4/7, and IgG3/5 of mares were significantly increased after VapA mRNA immunization and strongly correlated with the corresponding concentrations in their foals sera at age {approx}24 hours. Concentrations of anti-VapA IgGs remained increased in foals of vaccinated mares compared with control foals for at least 35 days.

abstract: Guanidine-bridged nucleic acid (GuNA) is a bridged nucleic acid analog with high binding affinity toward complementary strands along with high nuclease resistance. GuNA has been developed to improve pharmacokinetics and safety profiles of phosphorothioate modified gapmers. Here, we evaluated antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs) modified with combination of GuNA and 2'-O-methoxyethyl (MOE) and found that the dual-modification strategy could significantly improve knockdown activity in vitro and in vivo. Long-term efficacy evaluation showed that intracerebroventricularly administered GuNA-modified gapmers stayed active for over 24 weeks in mouse brain. Furthermore, we observed that GuNA-modified gapmers could evade lymphocyte-derived immune responses and kept ASO-induced toxicity in check. Taken together, the results of this study demonstrate that GuNA modification can improve the functional potential of ASOs, especially in the central nervous system.

abstract:
MOTIVATION: The interaction between RNA and proteins is a complex process that involves atom-level details and dynamic changes. Accurate prediction of protein-RNA interactions helps researchers to develop protein-targeted small nucleic acid drugs. However, the scarcity of protein-RNA complexes and experimental data limits the ability of existing data-driven supervised learning methods to learn latent patterns, leading to limited performance.
RESULTS: In this study, we propose PRIDA (Protein-RNA Interaction prediction based on Domain-Adversarial learning), a protein-RNA interaction framework that combines bilinear attention with conditional domain-adversarial learning. Powered by pretrained protein and RNA language models, PRIDA improves interaction prediction under protein-level distribution shifts and limited labeled data. By integrating PRIDA with Monte Carlo Tree Search, we apply it to a virtual screening pipeline to generate RNA aptamer candidates for specific target proteins. Experimental results show that PRIDA achieves state-of-the-art performance in cross-domain protein-RNA interaction prediction and provides effective guidance for RNA aptamer virtual screening.
AVAILABILITY: The data and source code of the proposed method are available at GitHub (https://github.com/zhouyyang/PRIDA) and Zenodo (https://zenodo.org/records/23644677).
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.

abstract: The goal of this study is to determine the safety and antitumor effects of REM-422, a MYB mRNA degrader, in people with Higher Risk MDS and relapsed/refractory AML
description:
This is a Phase 1, open-label, non-randomized, multicenter study investigating REM-422, a potent, selective, and oral small molecule mRNA degrader that reduces expression of the MYB transcription factor for patients with higher risk MDS or relapsed/refractory AML.

This study includes a Dose Escalation Phase and a Dose Expansion Phase. The purpose of the Dose Escalation Phase is to determine the maximum tolerated dose (MTD) and/or recommended Phase 2 dose (RP2D) of REM-422 in patients with higher risk MDS or relapsed/refractory AML. The purpose of Dose Expansion is to further evaluate the safety and anti-tumor activity of the RP2D carried forward from Dose Escalation.

Participation in this study will continue until disease progression, therapy intolerance, or participant withdrawal.

description:
This study is an open-label, two-arm, multi-step phase I study evaluating a combination of two broadly neutralizing antibodies (bNAbs), VRC07-523LS and PGT121.414.LS, in people living with HIV (PWH) who started antiretroviral therapy (ART) during acute/early infection. Participants will receive PGT121.414.LS and VRC07-523LS prior to undergoing an analytical treatment interruption (ATI). Participants will restart ART and continue follow-up after ATI to confirm viral suppression.

Participants will be screened for eligibility and have a pre-entry visit. After determination of eligibility, participants will be enrolled sequentially into Arm A (n=20) and then Arm B (n=20). The study consists of three steps including an analytic treatment interruption.

Arm A:

* Step 1: Participants remain on ART and will receive an infusion of VRC07-523LS and PGT121.414.LS at study entry.
* Step 2: Participants will interrupt their ART and receive a second infusion of VRC07-523LS 12 weeks after the initial infusion. Participants will be monitored closely for indications to resume ART.
* Step 3: Upon meeting ART restart criteria in Step 2; participants will resume ART and be followed for up to 24 weeks.

Arm B:

* Step 1: Participants remain on ART and will receive an infusion of VRC07-523LS and PGT121.414.LS at study entry and a second infusion of VRC07-523LS 12 weeks later.
* Step 2: Participants will interrupt their ART. Participants will be monitored closely for indications to resume ART.
* Step 3: Upon meeting ART restart criteria in Step 2; participants will resume ART and be followed for up to 24 weeks.

Participation in both arms will last up to 98 weeks.

abstract: mRNA-lipid nanoparticle (LNP) vaccines can elicit robust T cell responses; however, these responses remain insufficient, particularly in the context of cancer vaccine therapy. Although several types of adjuvants reportedly enhance T cell responses induced by mRNA-LNP vaccines, few comprehensive side-by-side comparisons exist, and it remains unclear which adjuvants are most suitable. Herein, we screened 15 adjuvants. The addition of class B CpG oligodeoxynucleotides (ODNs) markedly augmented T cell induction in an interleukin-12-dependent manner and promoted the antitumor effects of mRNA-LNP vaccines in mice. Class B CpG ODN-adjuvanted mRNA-LNP vaccines induced more potent T cell responses than the mRNA-LNP vaccine administered at a 10-fold higher dose, while exhibiting a more favorable safety profile. However, this approach also reduced the cellular uptake of mRNA-LNPs and antigen expression. As a possible mechanism underlying this reduced delivery efficiency, we found that class B CpG ODNs adsorbed onto LNPs and altered their particle characteristics. These findings demonstrate that supplementation with class B CpG ODN is a simple, safe, and readily implementable approach for enhancing mRNA-LNP vaccine-induced T cell responses. This study also highlights that adding auxiliary components to mRNA-LNPs can potentially affect the performance of LNPs as delivery carriers.

title: Enhancing mRNA-lipid nanoparticle vaccine-induced T cell responses by simple supplementation with class B CpG oligodeoxynucleotides.

abstract: Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1 virus has recently emerged in dairy cattle in the USA, leading to mastitis and sharp reductions in milk production. The main site of H5N1 viral replication is the mammary tissue rather than the respiratory tract and viral transmission between animals is thought to occur through viral shedding in milk. Here, we generate an mRNA-lipid nanoparticle (mRNA-LNP) vaccine encoding the hemagglutinin (HA) of A/dairy cattle/Texas/24-008749-002/2024, representative of circulating bovine H5N1 viruses, and assess its immunogenicity and efficacy in lactating dairy cows. Eight cows were divided into vaccinated and control groups, receiving two intramuscular doses of the vaccine or saline, followed by intramammary viral challenge. Vaccination elicited HA-reactive and neutralizing antibodies in serum and HA-reactive antibodies in milk. Following viral challenge, vaccinated cows had ~1,000-fold lower peak viral RNA in milk and a lower occurrence of mastitis and mammary fibrosis.

title: An mRNA-lipid nanoparticle vaccine against H5N1 influenza virus protects lactating dairy cows from infection.

abstract: The worldwide opioid epidemic continues to claim thousands of lives each year and remains one of the most urgent global public health challenges, driven by the high abuse potential and overdose risk of potent, fully synthetic μ-opioid receptor (MOR) agonists such as fentanyl. While fentanyl is highly effective in pain management, it also carries severe risks including respiratory depression, addiction, and fatal overdose. Understanding the neurobiological pathways underlying these risks is essential for developing safer analgesics and effective interventions. The MOR, a G-protein-coupled receptor (GPCR) that modulates neuronal excitability and synaptic transmission in important brain circuits like the ventral tegmental area (VTA), nucleus accumbens (NAc), and prefrontal cortex (PFC), is the primary receptor through which opioids exert their therapeutic effects. Dopaminergic dysregulation, transcriptional remodeling, and altered synaptic plasticity are neuroadaptations brought on by long-term opioid exposure that contribute to dependence and relapse. Life-threatening opioid toxicity is primarily driven by MOR-mediated suppression of respiratory networks, with risk shaped by dose, pharmacokinetics, receptor efficacy, and circuit sensitivity. Zebrafish (Danio rerio) provide a powerful complementary system for dissecting opioid-related neurocircuitry and screening for potential therapeutics. Zebrafish share conserved opioid-signaling components with mammals, and larval transparency facilitates in vivo imaging of neuronal activity at cellular resolution. Behavioral paradigms capture reward-related and drug-seeking phenotypes, while CRISPR-based approaches offer a means to investigate receptor-specific functions in validated models. In addition, zebrafish larvae provide an efficient platform for high-throughput screening of compounds that modulate opioid signaling and respiratory-related phenotypes. Together, insights from human, rodent, and zebrafish studies provide a more integrated understanding of opioid overdose and addiction neurobiology. This review incorporates current knowledge on the molecular and circuit-level mechanisms driving these processes and discusses how zebrafish models accelerate the discovery of safer analgesics and novel treatments for opioid use disorder and overdose.

title: Neurobiological Pathways Underlying Opioid Addiction and Overdose: Mechanisms, Therapeutic Targets, and Insights from Zebrafish Model.

abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to characterise the in vivo function of a murine regulatory region syntenic to the human rheumatoid arthritis (RA)-associated enhancer at the ACOXL locus and its role in immunity.
METHODS: Using CRISPR-Cas9, we generated the Bim-eΔ mouse model by excising a 15 kb genomic region syntenic to the human RA-associated locus tagged by rs13401811 from C57BL/6J zygotes. Bim expression was assessed by quantitative polymerase chain reaction. Thymocytes and splenocytes were profiled by flow cytometry, and whole-spleen RNA-seq was used to define transcriptional changes. Immune responses were tested using a Trichuris muris infection model and an antigen-induced arthritis (AIA) protocol.
RESULTS: Bim-eΔ mice show reduced Bim expression vs wild-type counterparts. This indicates that Bim is a transcriptional target of this region. Enhancer loss was correlated with differences in T cell proportions across age- and sex-stratified cohorts consistent with altered thymic selection. Splenic T and B cells were altered, and the transcriptome skewed toward inflammation. Bim-eΔ and wild-type mice mounted comparable responses to T. muris, whereas Bim-eΔ mice developed a severe adverse response during the sensitisation phase of the AIA protocol.
CONCLUSIONS: A murine noncoding regulatory region modulates Bim expression and immunity in vivo. Enhancer deletion altered the splenic transcriptional profile and lymphocyte composition while revealing a context-dependent phenotype upon inflammatory in vivo challenge. These findings support a role for RA-associated regulatory architecture in shaping immunity and point to BIM regulation as a potential therapeutic lever for restoring immune balance.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intraluminal obstruction produces chronic airway epithelial hypoxia. We investigated how chronic airway epithelial hypoxia and inflammatory stimuli interact in human bronchial epithelial (HBE) cultures and resected human bronchiectatic lungs to produce an airway epithelial environment characteristic of muco-obstructive disease.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: HBE cultures were exposed to normoxia or hypoxia (1% O2) for 5 days, followed by administration of supernatants from cystic fibrosis (CF) lung-derived mucopurulent material (SMM) or PBS for 24 h. A reverse order protocol with SMM followed by hypoxia was also performed. Bulk RNA-sequencing and functional (Na+ transport) studies were performed. HIF1A and EPAS1-mediated transcriptional responses were characterised in CRISPR knockdown HBE cells. RNA in situ hybridisation studies of excised bronchiectatic lungs and bioinformatic analyses of published datasets tested for relevance of in vitro findings to in vivo conditions.
RESULTS: Hypoxia and SMM regulated largely separate airway epithelial transcriptional programmes regardless of treatment order. PTGS2 (COX-2), CCL20, MUC5B, and CXCL8 (IL-8) represented a small number of genes upregulated by both hypoxia and SMM. HIF1A knockdown and EPAS1 knockdown produced distinct, often opposing, effects on hypoxia-responsive pathways. HIF1A dominated upregulation of glycolytic pathway signalling. EPAS1 regulated genes that increase mucus concentration under hypoxia (e.g., SCNN1G). An EPAS1 inhibitor blocked hypoxia-induced upregulation of Na+ transport.
CONCLUSION: Chronic hypoxia and inflammation regulated distinct genes/pathways that combine to produce a complex diseased environment in muco-obstructed airway epithelia. HIF1A and EPAS1 regulated distinct hypoxia-induced transcriptional responses. EPAS1 inhibition may exhibit a favourable therapeutic ratio for treatment of muco-obstructive lung diseases.

abstract: Patients with acute leukemias harboring translocations involving gene lysine methyltransferase 2A (KMT2A) have a poor prognosis due to chemotherapy resistance with rapid relapse following standard treatments. The resulting KMT2A fusion proteins dysregulate gene expression, leading to an upregulation of leukemogenic transcription factors such as HOXA9 and MEIS1, which drives leukemic transformation. Although menin inhibitors are proving to be promising new therapeutics for patients with KMT2A-rearranged (KMT2Ar) acute leukemia, resistance mechanisms have already been described and new therapeutic approaches for this patient subgroup must be identified. Here, a genome-wide CRISPR/Cas9 screen in a KMT2Ar B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia cell line identified the deubiquitinase ubiquitin-specific peptidase 22 (USP22) as a novel regulator of MEIS1 protein stability. USP22 is a member of the Spt-Ada-Gcn5 acetyltransferase multiprotein complex, which has crucial functions in shaping the chromatin landscape and modulating transcription. Genetic depletion of USP22 impaired cellular growth and proliferation in KMT2Ar acute leukemia models. Chromatin immunoprecipitation revealed cooperative binding between USP22 and MEIS1 at critical oncogenic target genes, suggesting that USP22 safeguards leukemogenic transcription by protecting MEIS1 from proteasomal degradation. Genetic or chemical inhibition of USP22 led to the polyubiquitination of MEIS1, resulting in proteasomal degradation and downregulation of the expression of target genes. Our study identifies USP22 as a novel regulator of MEIS1 protein stability that could potentially be exploited as a therapeutic target in the future in KMT2Ar leukemias.

title: USP22 is a novel vulnerability regulating MEIS1 protein abundance and gene transcription in KMT2Ar acute leukemia.

abstract: Due to the increasing demand for clinical gene therapy and the limitations of current treatment methods, there is an urgent need to develop gene-editing tools that are safer, more precise, and more clinically implementable. Deaminase-based base editors have emerged as gene-editing platforms with significant therapeutic potential because they can achieve precise single-base substitutions without inducing DNA double-strand breaks. However, the challenges of applying base editing in clinical practice extend beyond whether the intended edit can be achieved. The critical question is whether the editing system can reliably provide predictable, controllable, and verifiable outcomes across complex sequence contexts, diverse cell environments, and actual delivery conditions. This review focuses on the engineering optimization and clinical translation of base editors. We first systematically analyze the major factors affecting the clinical translation of base editors across four dimensions: editing efficiency, editing precision, safety, and delivery, together with the corresponding optimization strategies. We then summarize the applications of artificial intelligence and computational approaches in base editor design, screening, and risk assessment. We further discuss the ex vivo and in vivo pathways for clinical translation, including their respective requirements for product quality and safety evaluation. Finally, based on representative clinical programs, we discuss how editing performance, safety, and delivery factors influence development decisions for candidate base-editing systems across different therapeutic contexts, and propose minimum reporting recommendations to improve the consistency of key data and cross-study comparability.

abstract: Encapsulation efficiency (EE) estimates the encapsulated fraction of measured RNA in an mRNA lipid nanoparticle (LNP) preparation, whereas particle occupancy measures the fraction of particles containing detectable RNA. Neither metric describes the full distribution of RNA among particles. Particle-resolved studies show that high bulk EE can coexist with RNA-negative particles and broad copy-number distributions, but reported empty-particle fractions vary with composition, preparation, and analytical method. This Minireview examines fluorescence spectroscopy, particle-resolved microscopy and RNA counting, mass spectrometry, and population-separation approaches, distinguishing direct RNA-sensitive measurements from inferred loading. It considers manufacturing determinants and evidence linking payload distributions to product performance. Process changes can alter loading without parallel changes in mean particle size. mRNA-expression, multi-cargo gene-editing, and adjacent siRNA-knockdown studies suggest possible functional consequences, although the independent effect of binary occupancy on potency remains unresolved. Historical lipid-mediated delivery experiments caution against assuming that eliminating RNA-negative particles always improves activity. Occupancy is therefore best considered a context-dependent extended-characterization metric for development and comparability. Product-specific evidence is needed to determine whether occupancy is a critical quality attribute. Its use in routine testing would also require a fit-for-purpose validated analytical procedure and an appropriate control strategy.

abstract: Necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) is the most devastating gastrointestinal emergency in preterm infants, frequently causing mortality and long-term neurodevelopmental impairment1,2. Although the gut microbiota has been implicated in NEC pathogenesis3-5, the microbial factors driving NEC and the following brain pathology remain unclear. Here we identify Clostridium perfringens pathobionts containing Delta toxin in the gut microbiome of individuals with severe and fatal NEC. Clinically, infected infants show worse outcomes, including aberrant systemic inflammation, severe neurological damage and coagulopathy. We establish a mouse model in which Delta-toxin-positive C. perfringens infection, or Delta toxin exposure alone, recapitulates clinical features of NEC, including intestinal necrosis and acute cerebral injury. Mechanistically, Delta toxin preferentially targets macrophages, potently activating inflammasome signalling and pyroptosis, triggering a rapid inflammatory cascade that compromises blood-brain barrier integrity and drives neuroinflammation. Through a genome-wide CRISPR screen, we identify the tetraspanin CD9 as the host receptor for Delta toxin. Using systemic, myeloid-specific and intestinal-epithelial-specific Cd9-knockout mice, we show that systemic and myeloid Cd9 ablation protects mice against toxin-induced lethality, blood-brain barrier dysfunction and multiorgan injury, whereas epithelial Cd9 deletion shows partial protection, implicating macrophage targeting as a primary driver of C. perfringens CD9-dependent pathogenesis. Furthermore, a neutralizing anti-Delta toxin monoclonal antibody confers protection against disease progression. These findings suggest that a subset of NEC is a specific-toxin-mediated disorder and validate the Delta toxin-CD9 axis as a therapeutic target for this subset.

title: Clostridium perfringens Delta toxin targets CD9 to drive NEC and brain injury.

abstract: Zebrafish is an excellent in vivo model for high-throughput antiangiogenic drug testing, commonly known as the zebrafish angiogenesis assay. Conventional zebrafish angiogenesis assays are performed in wild-type zebrafish to evaluate the vascular changes in intersegmental and subintestinal vessel regions of the zebrafish larvae at 2 and 3 dpf stages, respectively. However, wild-type zebrafish larvae do not adequately mimic the hypoxia microenvironment and ectopic vessel branching characteristics of cancer. To overcome this limitation, we developed a genetically engineered zebrafish model with constitutive activation of the hypoxia signaling pathway by targeting the vhl, a tumor suppressor, by negative regulation of the hypoxia pathway, using CRISPR mutagenesis. This model exhibits robust ectopic blood vessel branching throughout the larval body, thereby recapitulating pathological angiogenesis. The utility of this zebrafish model system for drug screening was validated with the sorafenib treatment, a known antiangiogenic tyrosine kinase inhibitor. Overall, this proangiogenic hypoxia zebrafish model provides a physiologically relevant platform for testing antiangiogenic drugs. Key features • Generate a vhl mutant zebrafish line with constitutive activation of the hypoxia signaling pathway using CRISPR-CAS9 mutagenesis. • The generated model exhibits extensive ectopic neovascular branching and abnormal vascular growth resembling pathological angiogenesis observed in solid tumors. • Mimics the chronic hypoxic microenvironment commonly associated with cancer progression and angiogenesis. • Provides an economical alternative to mammalian tumor models for early-stage antiangiogenic drug testing.

abstract: Zuo1 slows elongating ribosomes in response to nascent peptide misfolding, which in turn triggers co-translational decay of the transcript. The endogenous substrates of this pathway have remained undefined. Using RNA-sequencing and ribosome profiling of unstressed wild-type and zuo1Δ cells, we identified transcripts that accumulate in the absence of Zuo1, representing mRNAs normally downregulated by Zuo1-mediated surveillance. Proteins encoded by these transcripts displayed higher predicted disorder across multiple metrics, were enriched in basic residues, were depleted of proline residues, and were shorter in length. Ribosome profiling revealed that Zuo1 target transcripts exhibited higher ribosome occupancy in the presence of Zuo1, and the ratio of wild-type to zuo1Δ ribosome occupancy positively correlated with predicted disorder. These findings indicate that Zuo1 surveillance acts preferentially on transcripts encoding nascent chains that fail to acquire stable structure.

abstract: Safflower is an Asteraceae oilseed crop valued for its high-quality unsaturated fatty acids (≈90% oleic and linoleic acids), natural floral pigments, and diverse bioactive compounds. These attributes underpin its applications in functional foods, nutraceuticals, pharmaceuticals, and various industrial sectors. Safflower inherent tolerance to drought, heat, cold, and salinity positions it as a climate-resilient alternative to more temperature-sensitive oilseeds; however, omics-based research in this crop remains comparatively fragmented. This review consolidates recent advances across major omics domains. Genomics covers chromosome-scale assemblies, GWAS panels, QTL mapping, and diagnostic candidate genes for molecular breeding. Transcriptomics summarizes regulatory networks for flavonoid and oil biosynthesis, stress-responsive transcription factors (NAC, WRKY, bZIP, AP2/ERF), and seed developmental programs. The proteomics section addresses stress-inducible, therapeutic, and storage/lipid metabolic proteins linked to quality and stress adaptation. Metabolomics outlines quinochalcone and flavonoid pathway architecture, color-specific metabolic profiles, and emerging clinical and nutraceutical applications. Phenomics highlights UAV-based high-throughput phenotyping, RGB and multispectral imaging for salt and drought screening, and machine-learning-assisted germplasm authentication. Epigenomics focuses on DNA methylation and miRNA-mediated regulation. Finally, lipidomics and metagenomics consider oil authentication biomarkers, refining optimization, and microbiome-driven nutrient cycling shaping medicinally important compounds. Despite these advances, critical gaps remain in multi-omics integration, CRISPR-based functional validation, genomic selection pipelines, and detailed characterization of root-shoot architecture under combined stresses. Addressing these gaps will advance mechanistic understanding of climate resilience and enable the development of stress-tolerant, high-yielding safflower cultivars with improved oil quality and bioactive profiles, thereby supporting climate-resilient production systems and high-value safflower-based products at scale.

abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) intracellular domains (ICDs) couple antigen recognition to T-cell activation. Here we worked with AI agents to refactor CAR ICDs, proposing designs and refining them as measurements accumulated over three rounds. This approach yielded KRGR-{zeta}1-40, a 45-amino-acid ICD less than a third the length of the clinical 4-1BB-CD3{zeta} (BB{zeta}) ICD. Compared with BB{zeta}, KRGR-{zeta}1-40 increased CAR surface expression and antigen-driven IFN-{gamma} release, without detectable antigen-independent IFN-{gamma} release. KRGR-{zeta}1-40 extended CAR expression and target-cell killing after transient mRNA delivery, supported the expression of four CARs from a shared mRNA dose, and enhanced B-cell depletion after lentiviral and lipid-nanoparticle delivery. These results show that iterative agent-guided design with experimental feedback can yield compact ICDs that enhance CAR expression and sustain CAR T-cell function.

outcomes.description: Fatigue will be assessed with the Functional Assessment of Chronic Illness Therapy-Fatigue subscale (FACIT-F). The FACIT-F Scale is a 13-item scale used to measure self-reported fatigue. Items are assessed on a 5-point Likert scale, with responses ranging from 0 for "not at all" to 4 for "very much". Relevant items are reverse scored, and all items are summed up to create a total score ranging from 0 to 52, with higher scores indicative of better functioning (i.e., less fatigue).

outcomes.description: The RAND KDQOL-36 is an abbreviated questionnaire that combines the generic and disease-specific components to assess participant's health-related quality of life. This 36-item questionnaire includes the RAND 12, Version 1 (12 items) and 3 disease-related domains, symptoms/problems (12 items), burden of kidney disease (4 items), and effects of kidney disease (8 items). It uses a recall of 4 weeks, and items are assessed on 3- to 5-point Likert scales or with a dichotomous response option. Higher score indicates better health. The raw scores are transformed linearly to a range of 0 to 100, with higher scores indicating better health.

abstract: Despite the remarkable clinical success of immunotherapy, its efficacy against hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains severely limited, highlighting an urgent need for novel targets and strategies to overcome immune evasion. Here, we aimed to identify key regulators of HCC immunity via unbiased functional screening and develop a targeted therapy to remodel the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME). We performed an in vivo CRISPR-knockout screen using a 4500-gene sgRNA library in syngeneic HCC mouse models. Single-cell RNA sequencing of human HCC tissues and in vivo macrophage-depletion assays were utilized to dissect cellular populations and validate underlying mechanisms. We identified ribosomal protein S19 (RPS19) as a central mediator of HCC immune evasion, whose deletion in HCC cells mitigates the immunosuppressive TME. Mechanistically, scRNA-seq pinpointed tumor-associated macrophages as the key effector subset, whereby complement C5a receptor 1 (C5aR1) transduces RPS19 signals to trigger macrophage-dependent immune suppression. We further constructed SP94-peptide-modified disulfide-bond-containing nanoparticles (SNPSS) for targeted CRISPR-Cas9 delivery. SNPSS efficiently homes to HCC cells, releases payloads within the glutathione-rich TME, downregulates RPS19, reverses immune suppression, and robustly suppresses HCC progression in vivo. Collectively, the RPS19-C5aR1-macrophage axis fuels HCC immune escape, and SNPSS-based RPS19 gene-editing offers a promising strategy to remodel the TME and boost HCC immunotherapy efficacy.

title: In Vivo CRISPR Screen Identifies RPS19 as an Immunotherapy Target in Hepatocellular Carcinoma.

abstract:
AIM: In vitro air-liquid interface (ALI) cultures of human airway epithelial cells are widely used to study respiratory biology and disease, as they recapitulate key features of the pseudostratified airway epithelium and reduce reliance on animal models and repeated patient biopsies. However, the limited proliferative capacity of primary airway basal cells restricts long-term studies and genome editing. This study aimed to generate stable, immortalised human airway basal cell lines that retain differentiation capacity and support genetic manipulation.
METHODS: Human airway epithelial basal cells from bronchial and nasal origin were immortalised by lentiviral expression of human telomerase reverse transcriptase (hTERT) followed by polyclonal expansion. A panel of cell lines derived from three independent nasal donors was established. Differentiation capacity was assessed in ALI cultures and compared with primary airway epithelial cells. Suitability for genetic manipulation was evaluated using lentiviral overexpression and CRISPR/Cas9-mediated gene knockout and knock-in strategies.
RESULTS: All immortalised cell lines displayed sustained proliferative capacity and efficiently differentiated into major airway epithelial cell types, including multiciliated and secretory cells. Differentiation patterns and functional characteristics closely resembled those of primary airway epithelial cultures. The cell lines supported efficient lentiviral transduction and CRISPR/Cas9-based genome editing, enabling stable gene overexpression, targeted gene disruption, and precise genomic modification.
CONCLUSIONS: hTERT-immortalised human airway basal cell lines preserve key features of primary airway epithelium while enabling long-term culture and versatile genome editing. This resource provides a robust platform for airway biology research, disease modelling, and therapeutic development.

abstract: A GGGGCC (G4C2) hexanucleotide repeat expansion in the first intron of C9orf72 is the most common monogenic cause of Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS) and Frontotemporal Dementia (FTD). This element serves as a template for repeat-associated non-AUG (RAN) translation, which generates neurotoxic dipeptide repeat (DPR) proteins that aggregate in patient brains and contribute to neurodegeneration in model systems. To understand the mechanisms underlying RAN translation initiation, we used cryo-electron microscopy to determine the structure of an in vitro assembled human late-stage C9orf72 translation initiation complex at 3.2 A resolution and a near-native complex purified from human cell lysate at 3.5 A resolution. RAN translation on C9orf72 mRNA initiates predominantly at a near-cognate CUG codon that is located 24 nucleotides upstream of the G4C2 repeat and is flanked by a strong endogenous Kozak sequence. The structures further reveal a direct interaction between the G4C2 repeat and 18S ribosomal RNA expansion segment 9 (ES9S) on the 40S small ribosomal subunit through a kissing-loop interaction. Preventing this RNA-RNA interaction using complementary antisense oligonucleotides significantly reduces RAN translation in vitro and in patient-derived iNeurons, indicating that this structural interaction is functionally important. These findings provide mechanistic insights into RAN translation initiation and highlight a novel potential therapeutic approach to mitigate toxic DPR production in C9orf72-associated neurodegenerative disease.

title: Structural basis for repeat-associated non-AUG translation initiation on C9orf72 mRNA

abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-engineered natural killer (NK) cell therapy has emerged as a promising immunotherapeutic strategy for cancer treatment, offering advantages over CAR-T cells such as a lower risk of cytokine release syndrome and graft-versus-host disease and the potential for off-the-shelf manufacturing. Viral vectors have long served as effective tools for CAR-NK engineering, but their dependence on complex manufacturing procedures, considerable production costs, and the potential risks associated with genomic integration has encouraged increasing interest in non-viral alternatives. Recent advances in genetic engineering technologies have facilitated the development of CAR-NK platforms, particularly through non-viral delivery approaches including electroporation, transposon systems and lipid nanoparticles, while CRISPR-based tools enable targeted genome editing. Meanwhile, an increasing number of clinical trials have begun to evaluate the safety and therapeutic potential of CAR-NK cells in both hematological malignancies and solid tumors. However, challenges such as limited NK-cell persistence, antigen heterogeneity, and the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment remain. In this review, we summarize recent progress in non-viral CAR-NK engineering strategies, analyze the current landscape of preclinical and clinical trials, and discuss key challenges and future directions for advancing CAR-NK therapy. Collectively, these advances suggest that non-viral engineering technologies may serve as an important technological foundation for next-generation CAR-NK therapies, enabling more flexible ex vivo manufacturing and potentially supporting the future development of in vivo CAR-NK generation strategies for solid tumors.

abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted global supply chains, causing shortages of critical lipid-based raw materials for mRNA vaccine production. To enhance formulation resilience, we systematically evaluated the impact of five ionizable lipids (ILs) on lipid nanoparticle (LNP) organization, mRNA delivery and immunogenicity. The physiochemical analysis revealed the potential coexistence of liquid crystalline lamellar (Lα) and inverse hexagonal (HII) phases, or a mixture of nucleotide-loaded and non-loaded HII phases within developed LNP formulations. Furthermore, ILs with saturated, multi-tail structures, such as Lipid-5 and SM-102, favored inverse hexagonal (HII) internal organization and fusion intermediates, correlating with enhanced endosomal fusion and higher in vivo protein expression. In contrast, ILs such as cKK-E12, which featured dual ionization headgroups and tended to form lamellar-like structures, showed reduced encapsulation efficiency and transfection potency. The preclinical experiments demonstrated that all developed formulations induced robust binding and neutralizing antibody responses; however, antibody responses were lower in mRNA Lipid 5 LNPs and mRNA SM-102 LNPs than in other formulations. Notably, within the limited panel of ILs in this study, protein expression levels did not show a clear correlation with antibody titers, highlighting that efficient antigen expression alone is not predictive of humoral immunity. These findings underscore how IL structural features influence LNP architecture and function, informing the rational design of next-generation mRNA vaccines.

title: Ionizable lipid impact on mRNA vaccine formulation properties and immunogenicity.

abstract: Chemical modifications of RNA bases and adenosine-to-inosine (A-to-I) editing are regulatory layers essentially unexplored in the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE), whose oxidative dysfunction underlies age-related macular degeneration. We mapped both layers in ARPE-19 cells exposed to tert-butyl hydroperoxide under two non-pharmacological interventions, Quantum Molecular Resonance (QMR) electrotherapy and a patient blood-derived secretome, across 56 libraries spanning four arms, three time points and matched stressed and stress-free conditions (GEO: GSE328981). Base modifications were called with HARMLNC and A-to-I editing screened with a transition-signal caller, then re-analysed with REDItools3, JACUSA2 and LoDEI. The high-confidence set comprised 241 calls at 15 sites, all of classes canonical to tRNA and rRNA. The most prevalent was an adenosine modification at chrM:2617 in mitochondrial 16S rRNA (MT-RNR2), detected in 51 of 56 libraries and in every arm. Two positions 1 bp apart lie in an EZR/SYTL3 overlap region, whereas a third chromosome 6 site maps to HLA-C, 127.5 Mb away. No position of either layer differed between treatment arms: 7 testable modification sites (minimum p = 0.19) and, at single-nucleotide resolution under dedicated callers agreeing to r = 0.975-0.992, 15 curated editing positions (minimum q = 0.169). Two one-sided tests bound any change in substitution composition within 1.4% and in mean editing frequency within 10% for secretome and combination and 20% for QMR. Against a stress-free baseline internal to the cohort, only chrM:13710 (MT-ND5) changed detectably (q = 0.03). These layers are therefore small, largely constitutive and quantifiably undisturbed by either intervention at the resolution available.
